holidays.name: National Chocolate Chip Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the tiny, melty chocolate nuggets that make cookies, pancakes, muffins and midnight snacks much better. Bake a batch of cookies, toss some chips into your trail mix, or just eat them straight from the bag. Nobody is watching.
holidays.origin: The holiday honors Ruth Wakefield, who is credited with inventing the chocolate chip cookie around 1938 at her Toll House Inn in Massachusetts. Nestlé later began selling chocolate morsels and printed her recipe on the package. It is an unofficial observance, and it has become a staple of American food calendars.
holidays.funFact: The chocolate chip cookie was a happy accident of the Toll House Inn kitchen, and it became so popular that Nestlé built its famous morsels around the recipe.

holidays.name: National Nylon Stocking Day
holidays.description: A salute to the sheer, stretchy leg-wear that changed fashion forever. Celebrate by pulling on a pair of stockings or tights, or by tipping your hat to the people who once lined up around the block to buy them.
holidays.origin: Nylon was introduced by DuPont in 1939, and nylon stockings went on sale nationwide in the United States on May 15, 1940. They were a durable, affordable alternative to silk, and the date is remembered as the day they reached the general public.
holidays.funFact: Nylon stockings were so wildly popular that shoppers swarmed stores to get a pair. The frenzy was nicknamed 'N-Day' and is remembered as the Nylon riots.

holidays.name: National Straw Hat Day
holidays.description: The unofficial start of warm-weather headwear season. Dust off your boater, fedora or sun hat, and wear it with pride at a picnic, a parade or just on the walk to the mailbox.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance welcoming summer, and it is listed on May 15 each year. It echoes an old fashion tradition in which straw hats were considered proper wear only after mid-May.
holidays.funFact: Straw hats once came with strict etiquette. Wearing one before the traditional mid-May start of summer was seen as a fashion blunder.
